searchText: nice read, thanks for writing that down, few questions/ideas that are not documented explicitly - (1) do you only intend to count faults on the canonical branch (your head) or also other branches (side chains)? - (2) how do you deal with self-build blocks that are not revealing the payloads, to whom do you attribute those? - (3) in lodestar, we seed the circuit breaker with randomness at startup, so it's not predictable by builders, do you think that makes sense? Thanks. 1) I'm not sure, whatever it's easier. I think we'll do this on any branch but the thing is that it'll naturally filter to just the canonical one by the condition that the block is strong 2) self built blocks don't play any role in this so they are ignored, I'll write this explicitly in this doc. 3) I thought about randomness and perhaps it's still worth it. But with per-builder filtering I think this is not that gameable. The biggest problem is if builders keep just behind a relay and depending on how they do it's harder to do per builder filtering. This is why I plan to be very aggressive trying to figure out which indices relays serve and at a fault from any builder in the relay they are all banned so builders should know that there's an extra risk that the whole relay will be banned if a single member fails to produce payloads > self built blocks don't play any role in this so they are ignored doesn't this add incentivizes for builders to use the blinded flow? I would at least think your `CriticalFailedBuilders` condition should also count self-build payloads that are not revealed/invalid, so you would a fallback to local building in that case too I don't think this is critical. The number of builder blocks is just too high, so it will be very noticeable if someone has forked clients to blind sign. In this case I'd reevaluate and patch Prysm quickly so you keep track in fork choice if payloads are self-build or from a builder? We don't yet actually, but yes, for the circuit breaker it'll most likely need the builder index at least to be tracked in forkchoice. Haven't really thought about implementation. Was going to do that today. Not sure if forkchoice or our Blockchain package is best. If I stick to canonical branch, just head would probably do bal-devnet-7 is also shutting down by EOD unless someone yells glam-devnet-6 has been axed. we're fine with shutting it down I want to test the circuit breaker soon (although probably not today) is there a chance of getting an endpoint working as a relay? Serving multiple bidding indices? I don't think we have any tools setup for this yet Also not sure if it should be in our scope of available tools tbh Didn't we want to configure multiple builder URLs directly in the VC? I remember there was a discussion around it with the outcome that mev-boost /the former relay) should be enshrined into clients Yeah that for sure, but I want a relay also instead of a builder. I want to make sure that I ban every single index when any of them fails to deliver can't you just ask all 4 builders and test the relay capabilities in prysm that way too? 😄 we can probably add a small tool , or add a relay to the buildoor instance overview. should be a claude one shot thingy, I'm just a bit worried that we're basically re-introducing something we wanted to get rid of intentionally yeah the trusted relay really doesn't need to exist if we have trusted builders no? just have prysm vc be able to handle a list of buildoor urls ? Also, the relay will only give you the best bid. So from prysm side, you should likely select a less valuable bid from another trusted builder if the bid from the first builder is rejected due to banning. The relay can't do that without also tracking the payload inclusion and doing the banning logic too? yeah I don't think we should be building/testing/encourage the use of any relays tbh what value do relays provide in Gloas? https://imgur.com/a/ZTmFknT Well while I fully agree with you, everything indicates that this is the most likely failure mode. And I want to be clear that Prysm will ban most likely the full relay (and possibly all relays if failing builders are represented in all relays and they're optimistically relayed) on the first offense, so I want this to be tested in full and not see surprises in mainnet I don't think we should wait to have relays testing this I would prefer to do it myself. I can try this on KT but I believe a full devnet is a better place for this Will have single builder circuit breaker soon and the relay integration shortly after does prysm have a way to list multiple builders? what does this question mean? a way to request from multiple builders? I don't think we have this yet cc <@363800010518822915> but notice that I am requesting the opposite here, I want to request from one endpoint that may return bids from different indices not return multiple bids, but return a different index on different slots yes we can support this, ill give you the kurtosis config in an hour. Have to drive somewhere ahh nice, I'm doing the trustless CB first, will move to trusted/whitelisted builders later and then finally to relays, so this can wait what’s the job of the relay here ? if you have list of trusted builders ? is it just for lazy ppl that want to specify a single url for all builders ? let's not get there, let's just assume they exist and they serve different indices from time to time. The ones that will take the blame when the chain halts will be us anyway so we need to test these paths bal-devnet-7 is now ded

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
nice read, thanks for writing that down, few questions/ideas that are not documented explicitly
- (1) do you only intend to count faults on the canonical branch (your head) or also other branches (side chains)?
- (2) how do you deal with self-build blocks that are not revealing the payloads, to whom do you attribute those?
- (3) in lodestar, we seed the circuit breaker with randomness at startup, so it's not predictable by builders, do you think that makes sense?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content:
Thanks. 
1) I'm not sure, whatever it's easier. I think we'll do this on any branch but the thing is that it'll naturally filter to just the canonical one by the condition that the block is strong 
2) self built blocks don't play any role in this so they are ignored, I'll write this explicitly in this doc. 
3) I thought about randomness and perhaps it's still worth it. But with per-builder filtering I think this is not that gameable. The biggest problem is if builders keep just behind a relay and depending on how they do it's harder to do per builder filtering. This is why I plan to be very aggressive trying to figure out which indices relays serve and at a fault from any builder in the relay they are all banned so builders should know that there's an extra risk that the whole relay will be banned if a single member fails to produce payloads

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content:
>  self built blocks don't play any role in this so they are ignored
doesn't this add incentivizes for builders to use the blinded flow? I would at least think your `CriticalFailedBuilders` condition should also count self-build payloads that are not revealed/invalid, so you would a fallback to local building in that case too

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: I don't think this is critical. The number of builder blocks is just too high, so it will be very noticeable if someone has forked clients to blind sign. In this case I'd reevaluate and patch Prysm quickly

excerpts.author: nflaig
excerpts.content: so you keep track in fork choice if payloads are self-build or from a builder?

excerpts.author: potuz
excerpts.content: We don't yet actually, but yes, for the circuit breaker it'll most likely need the builder index at least to be tracked in forkchoice. Haven't really thought about implementation. Was going to do that today. Not sure if forkchoice or our Blockchain package is best. If I stick to canonical branch, just head would probably do
